0.original: Ketenramm is considering your next steps.

48.original: The Forked Towers are the largest structures on the island. As such, they also store the lion's share of knowledge and relics.

49.original: The towers may have helped shape the Occult Crescent as we know it, but that is not the whole story...

50.original: So, the isle's aetherial currents are in disarray...

51.original: Come to think of it, the landscape here is completely different to what we saw down south. It feels warped─unnatural even.

52.original: We ought to investigate what caused those changes.

53.original: And I suggest we start by surveyin' multiple confluences. That should give us a clearer picture of what's happenin' at the aetherial level.

54.original: I've a mind to accompany you on your excursion. That way I can immediately share what the seal's undoing reveals at each site.

55.original: No need to pay me any heed, though. In the interest of avoiding my untimely demise at the hands of some fell fiend, I shall follow stealthily at a safe distance.

56.original: In that case, I'll stay put. I suggest ye concentrate yer search on the ruins in the area, and check for any abnormalities.

57.original: Judgin' by our scouts' reports, the ambient aether is densest around the ruins. Methinks they'll be yer best bet for findin' any confluences.

58.original: I've no idea why, but I've become rather adept at skulking through the shadows since being afflicted thus. You shan't even know I'm following you!

59.original: I think I shall join you too...

60.original: This sprawling structure bears all the hallmarks of Skallic craftsmanship, but my eye is drawn to the extensive flooding...

61.original: A surfeit of water-aspected aether appears to have disrupted the area's natural balance.

62.original: Hmmm. One of the crew told me that the ancient city of Skalla now lies at the bottom of a loch.

63.original: Though I state the obvious, 'twas not always so. The city's submerged state is the result of a calamitous flood─not some architectural quirk.

64.original: In other words, if one sought a faithful reproduction of Skallic civilization as it stood in the Fifth Astral Era, replicating the subsequent flood would be completely anachronistic...

65.original: Well, at least we have further evidence of aetherial abnormalities. Onward, to the next ruin!

66.original: Well, I've now seen enough to support my hypothesis, and I imagine Ketenramm will wish to hear of it too. Let us return to the camp posthaste.

67.original: Ah, not even the ravages of time can dim the allure of Nymian ingenuity.

68.original: Of course, the Nym of my time was not so...unconcerned with gravity.

69.original: This strange, floating aspect was not an inherent feature of the city. Though, having examined the confluence, the underlying phenomenon is clear.

70.original: Excess wind energies have weakened the bonds between building and ground, creating the landscape you see before you.

71.original: Intriguingly, this result seems somehow intentional... But that hardly aligns with the goal of accurately preserving Fifth Astral Era history.

72.original: Alas, there's not much else to glean from this confluence. Let us seek out other ruins!

73.original: Well, I've now seen enough to support my hypothesis, and I imagine Ketenramm will wish to hear of it too. Let us return to the camp posthaste.

74.original: <cough> Something tells me we ought not linger here...

75.original: Thankfully I was able to examine several aetherial flows en route. Something has sapped the area's earth-aspected energies, leading to a decline in the purifying potential of the soil, and a veritable mold invasion!

76.original: Now, I understand that the Lost City of Amdapor is likewise riddled with rot. Yet I find it difficult to believe those moldering forces could sweep as far as here.

77.original: Not only is the North Horn isolated from the rest of the isle, the Occult Crescent itself is malms away from the nearest port. Besides, if those foul spores <hex:021A020203>had<hex:021A020103> somehow spread here, I would expect the entire region to be infested...

78.original: At least we are beginning to glimpse the sheer extent of the environmental decay. 'Tis fortunate the nearby aetherial currents were still somewhat detectable.

79.original: On that note, I suggest we take our leave of these streets before we ourselves sprout moldy growths! More ruins─<cough>─await!

80.original: Well, I've now seen enough to support my hypothesis, and I imagine Ketenramm will wish to hear of it too. Let us return to the camp posthaste.

81.original: On this occasion, I scarcely need to examine the confluence─it is all too clear the vicinity is being subsumed by the void.

82.original: In ancient Mhach, mages would infuse their ceremonial chambers with astral-aspected aether to facilitate their summoning arts.

84.original: But that's not to imply the city was overrun with summoned voidsent. If this settlement lies in such a state, it can only mean one thing...

86.original: My theories can wait, however. There are more ruins to explore!

87.original: Well, I've now seen enough to support my hypothesis, and I imagine Ketenramm will wish to hear of it too. Let us return to the camp posthaste.

88.original: You know, I watched the Archive head back to camp from up here. He was threadin' his way through packs of fiends with surprisin' grace!

89.original: The Archive's seal continues to crumble...

90.original: Phew! That was quite the journey. I'm not sure I'd have made it without you.

91.original: Now, all the ruins we saw exhibited aetherial abnormalities.

92.original: The Nymian remains now float skyward due to excess wind energies, and the Skallic structure was inundated with water, while the Amdapori and Mhachi remnants are beset by earth- and astral-aspected imbalances, respectively. I also sense that the area surrounding the camp has been parched dry by an excess of fire-aspected aether...

93.original: In short, the aetherial balance of the North Horn has completely collapsed.

94.original: I believe the architect used the region to model the impact of such drastic aetherial changes.

96.original: The ruins here met a similar fate to their Eorzean counterparts.

97.original: It's as if he intentionally replicated the wounds inflicted during the War of the Magi...

98.original: To what end the architect conducted this experiment, I do not know. But these conditions stem from excessive use of aether in accordance with each civilization's unique history.

99.original: Perhaps disruptin' the flow of aether to the Tower of Magic was part of his plan, then? Not that I have the foggiest idea <hex:021A020203>why<hex:021A020103> he'd want to...

100.original: Nor have I. To jeopardize precious remnants of the Fifth Astral Era in this way contradicts the isle's very purpose...

101.original: Regardless, if your theory is correct, I'm afraid we'll have a difficult time tracking down the tower via aetherial flows. Though the fact the pavilion exists at all ought to provide <hex:021A020203>some<hex:021A020103> encouragement...

102.original: Are ye suggestin' there might be an aetherial node and means of activatin' it after all?

103.original: Heh. I love a good mystery as much as the next fellow, but we're practically drownin' in the bleedin' things!

104.original: Anyroad, before we get to solvin' them, I reckon we ought to take stock of what we've gleaned so far.
